name: Weather
description: The weather where you are, from the service you trust, with alerts when it turns bad
complete-description:
See the weather for any place at a glance: the temperature, what it's doing outside, what it feels like, today's high and low, and more. Each widget is named after its place, so a Regina widget is simply called Regina.

Pick where the weather comes from. Open-Meteo works anywhere in the world and is the default. If you live in Canada, Norway or the US, you can use your own country's weather service instead: Environment Canada, MET Norway or the US National Weather Service. Those three also send weather alerts, which pop up on the screen once each, with a code you can scan to read more. You choose how serious an alert has to be before it shows. OpenWeatherMap and Google Weather are there too if you have a key for them, and Google Weather sends alerts as well.

You decide what matters most. Drag the Info order into the order you like: the top one shows even on the smallest tile, and bigger tiles show more. Temperature can be in Celsius or Fahrenheit, and wind in km/h or mph. If the service can't be reached for a while, the last reading stays up, marked as the last known one, and the tile always names where its weather came from.

What it needs from you: a place. It uses OmniCore's location unless you search for a city. Open-Meteo, Environment Canada, MET Norway and the US National Weather Service need nothing else, no account and no key. Each of the three national services only works for places in its own country, and the tile says so if you pick one for somewhere else. OpenWeatherMap needs your own free API key, and Google Weather needs your own key from Google Cloud. When you pick either, it asks for the key.
